errors: Condition (b) as transcribed says the D_i are 'mutually disjoint 2 by 2' yet pass through a common vertex t. This is contradictory unless it means the points s are pairwise distinct, or disjointness away from t. It is likely a transcription or wording slip.

Condition (a) implicitly requires that no other chord crosses the fan t–σ, so that each t s s' is really a cell. Grothendieck asserts uniqueness of the triangles rather than deriving it from (a)–(c). This is a small gap but true for genuine pseudo-line arrangements.
Because ∂Δ double-covers L, the antipodal image of σ also lies under the chords through t. One must specify that the fan condition holds on one side only; the text is ambiguous here.
The definition of exceptional arcs is left fragmentary and heavily crossed out on this page.

ideas.what: Cutting RP² along a pseudo-line L to get a disc whose boundary is the double cover of L, with the other pseudo-lines becoming antipodal chords; parallel classes correspond to vertices of Σ on L
ideas.modern_name: Disc/chord model of a pseudoline arrangement relative to a line (related to wiring diagrams and allowable sequences)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Goodman–Pollack (allowable sequences, 1980s); folklore since Levi 1926 / Ringel 1956

ideas.what: Specialization triangle: the fan of cells with apex a vertex t, all of whose lines cross L consecutively without intervening lines; L can be pushed through t
ideas.modern_name: Triangle flip / mutation (Ringel), non-simple version; covering relation in the poset of single-element extensions (cocircuit signatures)
ideas.usually_credited_to: G. Ringel (1956); Las Vergnas (single-element extensions, 1978); Bokowski–Sturmfels; Sturmfels–Ziegler 1993 (extension spaces)

ideas.what: Generalization vs specialization arcs on L̃ as local charts of the possible transitions of the relative position of L
ideas.modern_name: Local structure (star of a vertex) of the extension space / poset of single-element extensions of a rank-3 oriented matroid

ideas.what: Exceptional specialization arcs (L degenerating towards a line of Σ through a vertex on L), with endpoints in a single parallel class
ideas.modern_name: Degenerate extension where the new element becomes parallel to (coincides with) an existing element

missed.claim: Grothendieck develops (1983–84) a systematic local combinatorics of how the relative position of a moving pseudo-line L changes. The double cover L̃ is decomposed into generalization, ordinary/exceptional specialization and inaction arcs forming 'characteristic polygons', with disjointness and adjacency theorems. This is a hand-made theory of the extension space of rank-3 oriented matroids, a decade before Sturmfels–Ziegler. The explicit arc/polygon classification on L̃, especially the exceptional arcs, is not something I recognise in the literature in this form.
missed.quote: La réunion de tous ces triangles s'appelle un triangle de spécialisation. Sa base ... est appelée un arc de spécialisation (ordinaire)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Rank-3 extension spaces are connected and well studied, but a clean local 'characteristic polygon' description of the link of an extension, including degenerate (exceptional) moves, could be useful for flip-graph and mutation-graph computations. It also documents Grothendieck's independent oriented-matroid work.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics largely rediscovers known oriented-matroid and pseudoline-flip theory (Ringel flips, single-element extensions). The arc classification on L̃ and the exceptional specialization arcs are a somewhat original local formalism, but they are fragmentary and of modest novelty. The historical interest (Grothendieck independently building extension-space combinatorics in 1983–84) is the main point.
